name: Limbe Botanic Garden & Black Sand Beach
description: A lush botanical garden founded in 1892 sitting right above Limbe's volcanic black-sand coastline, with views of Mount Cameroon rising behind the Atlantic.

name: Mount Cameroon
description: West Africa's tallest peak and an active volcano, offering a multi-day trek through rainforest, savanna, and volcanic scree to a 4,040m summit.

name: Waza National Park
description: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in the Sahelian north, home to elephants, giraffes, lions, and hundreds of bird species across open savanna.

name: Rhumsiki (Mandara Mountains)
description: A village in the volcanic Mandara Mountains famous for its dramatic rock spires, Kapsiki culture, and traditional crab-divination ceremonies.

name: Foumban Royal Palace & Museum
description: Seat of the Bamoun Kingdom since the 14th century, with a royal museum housing masks, thrones, and artifacts spanning centuries of Bamoun history.

name: Kribi Beach & Lobe Waterfalls
description: White-sand Atlantic beaches meet the rare sight of the Lobe Falls cascading directly into the ocean, just south of Kribi town.

name: Dja Faunal Reserve
description: A UNESCO World Heritage rainforest reserve, one of the largest and best-protected in Africa, home to gorillas, chimpanzees, and forest elephants.

name: Yaoundé — Seven Hills Capital
description: Cameroon's hilltop capital, home to the striking Reunification Monument, the National Museum, vibrant markets, and a growing food and nightlife scene.

name: Douala — Economic Capital
description: Cameroon's largest city and main port, known for its energetic street food scene, art galleries, and the lively Akwa nightlife district.

name: Bafut Palace
description: The traditional seat of the Fon of Bafut, a UNESCO-tentative-list palace complex of carved wooden buildings reflecting Grassfields kingdom heritage.

name: Buea Waterfalls
description: A refreshing cascade on the lower slopes of Mount Cameroon near Buea, a popular short hike for travelers based in the mountain-foot town.

name: Ekom-Nkam Falls
description: A dramatic 80-meter waterfall on the Nkam River made famous by Hollywood's Greystoke (Tarzan) film, framed by dense rainforest.

name: Bamenda — Grassfields Capital
description: The Northwest Region's hilltop capital, known for the dramatic Bamenda Ring Road escarpment views and vibrant Grassfields culture.

name: Dschang & Lake Baleng
description: A cool highland town nicknamed Cameroon's Switzerland, near the volcanic crater Lake Baleng and popular hiking trails through tea plantations.

name: Mefou National Park (Primate Sanctuary)
description: A primate rescue sanctuary just outside Yaoundé, home to gorillas, chimpanzees, and mandrills rescued from the bushmeat and pet trade.

name: Korup National Park
description: One of Africa's oldest and most biodiverse rainforests, with a famous 200m suspension bridge walk through the canopy.

name: Maroua — Sahel Crossroads
description: A Sahelian trading city known for its leather crafts, vibrant markets, and as the gateway to Mandara Mountains excursions.

name: Ngaoundéré Lamido's Palace
description: The traditional palace of the Lamido (Fulani ruler) of Ngaoundéré, offering a window into Adamawa's pastoral Fulani heritage.

name: Lake Nyos
description: A striking volcanic crater lake in the Oku volcanic field, dramatic and remote, best visited with a local guide.

name: Bafoussam — Bamiléké Heartland
description: The West Region's commercial hub and gateway to Bamiléké chiefdom villages, known for its markets and nearby traditional chefferies.
